classification.difficultyReason: The steps are stepped out: substitute x=12 into two expressions, add the results, and conclude. The only conceptual step is using the converse of the co-interior angle property, which is cued by the prompt. This needs a little more than a single direct application but has no algebraic proof of the kind in p49-q16.

content.prompt: Use co-interior angles to show that $AB$ is parallel to $DC$ when $x=12$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence show that $AB$ is parallel to $DC$.

answer.short: $110^{\circ}+70^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$, so the co-interior angles sum to $180^{\circ}$ and $AB\parallel DC$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC+\angle BCD&=110^{\circ}+70^{\circ}\\&=180^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The co-interior angles sum to $180^{\circ}$, so $AB$ is parallel to $DC$ by the converse of the co-interior angle property.
